newsitem.title: INDIA: Japan aid agency head sees yen depreciating.
newsitem.headline: Japan aid agency head sees yen depreciating.

text.p: CALCUTTA, India, Oct 4 (Reuter) The chief of Japan's aid agency, the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OECF) in India, said on Friday that the yen was declining and expected to depreciate further in the next decade.
"As of now yen is depreciating. And it is expected to depreciate further because of the ageing problem of our population," Yoshitaro Fuwa told reporters in Calcutta.
A rise in the number of aged would lead to a decline in savings and erode the strength of the yen, he said.

"It will benefit the Third World countries as they will have to repay their loans with interest only in yen," Fuwa said after addressing an international conference on financing infrastructure projects in the eastern Indian city.

In India, the OECF was holding negotiations with authorities to provide yen loans to private sector firms through financial institutions for investment in the infrastructure sector including power transmission and distribution, he said.
